newsitem.title: UK: Tajik rebel leader agrees to talks - TASS.
newsitem.headline: Tajik rebel leader agrees to talks - TASS.

text.p: Tajik rebel leader Makhmud Khudoyberdyev has announced the withdrawal of his forces from some areas and agreed to talks with Tajikistan authorities, Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said in a report monitored by the BBC on Wednesday.

"Khudoyberdyev has announced that his force withdraws from fighting on the Fakhrobad pass and in other areas. He has issued a statement of consent to meet delegates of the Tajik leadership for talks at any time and place," the agency said.

It quoted one of Khudoyberdyev's advisers as saying the rebel leader had taken the decision in order to avoid further casualties and because the proximity of a fertiliser factory meant an explosion could cause a serious environmental disaster.
No independent confirmation of the report was immediately available.

Burning fields saw Tajikistan's hard won peace go up in smoke on Tuesday as government forces in the former Soviet republic rocketed positions held by Khudoyberdyev, a mutinous colonel, south of the capital Dushanbe.

Clouds of acrid brown smoke hung over the Fakhrobad valley as the presidential guard, loyal to Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov, unleashed Grad rockets against troops fighting for the renegade colonel.
Rakhmonov's spokesman, Zafar Saidov, told Reuters earlier in Dushanbe that the president and Khudoyberdyev had agreed to meet during a late night telephone conversation.
"Rakhmonov and Khodoyberdyev spoke by telephone last night. Both sides have said the conflict can only be resolved by peaceful means," he said.
Saidov said it had been quiet overnight in the Fakhrobad valley, 25 km (15 miles) south of Dushanbe, where government forces clashed with Khudoyberdyev's troops on Tuesday.

Khudoyberdyev, 34, commander of an elite government armoured brigade who has mutinied twice before in as many years, moved his armour towards Dushanbe at the weekend in the wake of fighting between two rival warlords in the capital, one of whom appears to be backing the government now.
